html:
SMTO-GWT-0028 — SMTO doesn't know how to reach this computer yet

GUID: d6a0355b-406a-427e-9c0b-cf3c88374f80
Slug: gateway-node-unresolved
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gwt

What happened

  • The computer you chose is listed in SMTO, but SMTO has not yet learned its network name, so it can't send work there. Your request was not sent to it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the computer is on and connected to the network, and that its Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses to run work there) is running. SMTO learns the computer's name from the Gateway itself, so the Gateway must be reachable.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, find that computer and select Check connection. A successful check saves the computer's network name so SMTO can route work to it.
  3. If the check still fails, ask the person who installed that Gateway for its node name. Select Edit, type it in the Node field, then select Save changes. The node name tells SMTO exactly which Gateway program to talk to on that computer.
  4. Send your request again. If an earlier Task was already running on that computer, check its results first. Losing track of a computer does not prove that earlier work there didn't run, so checking avoids doing it twice.

What success looks like

  • In the Gateways list the computer shows Connected and a Node line, and your Task starts running on it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, together with the Gateway's startup messages, to the person who set up that Gateway. Don't delete and re-add the Gateway while Tasks or schedules still use it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway routing found the selected or prompt-named Gateway record, but it has no resolved node or usable base URL, so no execution context or terminal endpoint could be built.

What this means

  • A selected or nickname-matched Gateway exists but cannot supply a usable execution context, node or terminal endpoint. Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.

Why this can happen

  • A selected or nickname-matched Gateway exists but cannot supply a usable execution context, node or terminal endpoint.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the selected record's resolved node and transport-specific endpoint or outbound session.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the Gateway record's node, base_url and transport (execution_scope._gateway_context_from_record returns nothing when either node or base_url is empty). Run Check connection so the health probe stores the node reported by the Gateway's /capabilities response, or set the record's Node field to the Gateway's GATEWAY_NODE_NAME; for an outbound Gateway, confirm its hello includes a node and the session is connected.
  • Refresh the Gateway connection and verify its node and identity before submitting work.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The same verified Gateway yields a complete execution context and terminal route when needed.

What not to do

  • Do not treat a lost connection as proof that earlier remote work did not run.

Technical notes

  • Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
